segments.text: Welcome to the daily Robotics news digest for October 4th, 2026.
We're diving into updates on the latest humanoid advancements, ROS releases, and important calibration challenges.
From Humanoids Daily, RoboParty Unveils RP1 Humanoid at IROS, Plans Broader Open-Source Release in Q4.
This report details the unveiling of the RP1 humanoid robot at IROS and its demonstrated capabilities.
At the event on September 28th, the RP1 humanoid robot was presented, showcasing advanced balance recovery capabilities and the ability to achieve peak joint torques up to 160 Newton-meters.
The company has scheduled broader releases of the RP1, including the full stack, for the fourth quarter.
Plans involve the progressive release of motion control, simulation environments, software development kits, and PartyOS to the community.
Developers are directed to the earlier ROBOTO ORIGIN repository for initial resources.
This progression indicates an increased focus on democratizing access to advanced humanoid robotics technology within the development community.
From Planet ROS, "ROS Discourse General: RobotCAD v12.10.0 is released!".
This report details the release of RobotCAD version twelve point ten point zero, introducing several new features and necessary fixes.
The update includes a new RobotCAD MCP server designed for agentic robot assembling and an updated Models Library featuring faster import capabilities for xacro and mjcf models.
Additionally, the release incorporated a sensors field of view feature and enhanced compatibility for external document links and coordinate systems.
Support was also added for the Sverk aerial robot framework and a vacuum gripper tool for Gazebo.
This update signals continued development in robotics simulation and software tooling.
Further developments in agentic systems and simulation environments are anticipated.
From Planet ROS, "ROS Discourse General: Has anyone found a reliable way to validate a hand eye calibration result?".
This report addresses the ongoing challenge of establishing a reliable method for validating hand-eye calibration results within the robotics community.
Existing tools provide reprojection error or transform data, but a consensus on trusting these results remains absent.
Visual inspection within visualization environments like RViz is noted as insufficient for proper validation, particularly concerning scale.
The author seeks practical methods, such as validation motions or comparison against measured poses, that bypass the need for expert judgment.
The community requires the establishment of a standardized procedure for confirming the accuracy of these calibration results.
This pursuit is essential for advancing the trustworthiness of spatial data in robotics applications.
From Planet ROS, "ROS Discourse General: Tuning StereoSGBM on PS5 Camera (ROS 2 Galactic) for Dense Depth Maps"
reports on an attempt to tune StereoSGBM parameters within ROS 2 Galactic for dense depth map estimation from a PlayStation 5 stereo camera.
The core finding involves difficulties in achieving smooth depth maps, as parameter adjustments resulted in outputs that were either overly sparse or excessively noisy.

The methodology involved tuning settings such as the correlation window size, uniqueness ratio, and speckle settings in an effort to produce a point cloud suitable for 3D reconstruction using RTAB-Map.
Attempts to refine the process indicated that missing pre-filtering steps or specific calibration issues related to the camera setup may be influencing the inconsistent results observed.
This research suggests that specific hardware calibration and pre-processing are critical for reliable depth map generation from consumer camera systems.
And that's all the circuits for today's robotics roundup!
From RoboParty's new RP1 to open-source dreams, keep those gears turning.
Have a fantastic rest of your day!
